title: Pre-SIEM Detection for Financial Services
content_md: tl;dr Prime Detect runs detection rules on your event stream before data reaches the SIEM. It applies Sigma rules to events in transit, tags each match with a severity and a MITRE ATT&CK technique, and links related matches into attack chains. In client testing, about 7% of telemetry was tagged. That is the slice worth sending to your SIEM. Large organizations use Prime Detect to run 20,000+ detections without SIEM rule limits, cut what they pay to ingest, and keep a mapped record of what they detect for regulations such as DORA and NYDFS. It works alongside your existing SIEM. It does not replace it. Contact Sales Why banks are moving detection ahead of the SIEM A SIEM runs detection rules against data it has already ingested and indexed. For a large bank, that model hits two limits. Rule capacity. Most SIEM deployments run a few hundred active rules before search performance and cost become a problem. A team running 500 of them is choosing what not to see. Ingest cost. Every event the SIEM ingests is an event you pay to store and search, whether or not it carries a threat signal. Prime Detect moves detection upstream. Rules run against events as they stream through your Kafka pipeline, before ingest. Rule count is tied to the compute you give it, not to SIEM capacity. You then decide what reaches the SIEM based on what the rules found. Regulators set the floor. DORA Article 10 requires mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activity.
